technical_validation.duplicate_guard_evidence: r4 checkpoint/rebuild paths reject duplicate ownership; current registry read found one owner per frozen target.
technical_validation.qualification: Mutable global registry was read only for ownership and not hash-locked.

items.evidence: Paragraph 180 states broad remedy discretion under FCA 18.1(3) and discretionary costs governed by Rule 400(3) factors and other relevant matters.
items.scope_review: Qualification: broad does not mean unfettered, and this paragraph does not award a specific amount. The Rule 400 constraint is preserved.

items.evidence: Paragraph 15 compares allegation seriousness and evidentiary strength among individuals.
items.scope_review: It states neither a legal standard of proof nor an innocence holding.

items.evidence: Paragraph 111 attributes to the Supreme Court the CHRC filtering role under the CHRA: referral screening rather than rights determination.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is cited-court authority and CHRA-specific. It must not be transferred to the PSEA Commission or treated as a procedural-fairness exemption.

items.evidence: Paragraph 3 accurately states the three alternative PSEA grounds and their corresponding sections 66-69.
items.scope_review: The after-investigation and Commission-satisfied conditions are explicit; this is not a claim that every ground exists in this case.

items.evidence: Paragraph 126 concludes that section 69 fraud powers and their impact on individuals justify greater procedural protection.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is tied to the fraud seriousness and individual-impact context after the Baker analysis; it does not specify one universally mandatory procedure.

items.evidence: Judgment points 1-4 support relief/fairness, point 5 separately supports costs, and point 6 separately supports finality.
items.scope_review: The three evidence spans are pairwise disjoint. Relief remains limited to effects on the applicant; $650 is deducted only if not already paid; finality begins only upon expiry of appeal rights. Editor credit is excluded.

items.evidence: Paragraph 12 reports investigator findings about deceit, job title, working relationship and credibility.
items.scope_review: Agency findings are not current-court guilt or credibility adjudication and do not state a general fraud test.

items.evidence: Paragraph 52 reports a dictionary definition quoted in the investigator's report.
items.scope_review: The lexical source is not a distinct current-court legal definition in this target. The court's later analysis in paragraph 53 is outside this target and is not negated.

items.evidence: Paragraph 153 recounts reference-checking, examination/interview and e-mail history.
items.scope_review: It formulates no general reference rule or court fraud finding.

items.evidence: Paragraph 83 describes sections 66-68 appointment remedies for selection-affecting error, omission, improper conduct or political influence.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the proposition is confined to sections 66-68. It does not decide an independent section 69 corrective power against a third party; paragraphs 84, 93 and 183-184 preserve that unresolved question.

boundaries.note: Only frozen tenth10 decisions are accepted; mutable overall progress is outside scope.
